Village Craft Guide

Five Krownlandia village traditions to explore without the 3D park. Try the paper exercises in any order, or describe your designs aloud. They award no points and do not change your park progress.

  • Riverbend: pottery and baskets
  • Eldergrove: wooden plaques
  • Stonehearth: stone patterns
  • Meadowbrook: weaving
  • Whispering Pines: pinewood inlay

Riverbend: pottery and baskets

The recorded Riverbend village description includes pottery and woven baskets (page 3). In the park, Discover Riverbend offers both practices.

Try it on paper: Outline a bowl or a vase. Give it a repeating band of dots or waves. For a basket instead, number four bands from bottom to top, choose light or dark for each, and add a low or arched handle.

Eldergrove: wooden plaques

The recorded Eldergrove description includes woodcraft. In the park, the woodcraft shelter offers Woodcraft practice.

Try it on paper: Choose an oval or square plaque. Place a leaf or branch motif inside it. Describe the shape and motif so someone could imagine your design without seeing it.

Stonehearth: stone patterns

The recorded Stonehearth description includes stone architecture and masonry. Its courtyard offers Arrange a stone pattern.

Try it on paper: Make a two-by-two grid. Label each tile smooth or striped. Say the four choices in reading order: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.

Meadowbrook: weaving

The recorded Meadowbrook description includes textiles, natural dyes, and weaving (page 2). Search the park map for Meadowbrook weaving table if you want to try the in-park sampler.

Try it on paper: Draw six rows. Choose rose or gold for each row, or write the color names instead. Try a repeating sequence, then change one row and describe what changed.

Whispering Pines: pinewood inlay

The recorded village description includes woodworking and resin crafts. In the park, the story board and bench offer Pinewood inlay practice.

Try it on paper: Draw three slots labeled left, center, and right. Pick pinewood or amber for each. Try matching the outer slots and using the other material in the center. This is a design exercise with imaginary materials.

The recorded village descriptions are the inspiration. The workshop layouts, choices, and paper exercises are interpretations made for this prototype.
